# bubbletea answers async.do by posting the closure back through Update
# (#272), so a query whose fetch waits runs there: the wait is on a goroutine,
# and what the mount writes after it lands in the Model the loop owns. The
# latest attempt wins and an unmounted query's answer lands nowhere, as on
# every other target.
#
# A query in a component built per copy of a loop -- a card per row -- keeps
# its state in a cell per copy, and its effect is keyed on the pair of the
# copy and its own key, so each row asks for its own and a row whose key
# changes asks again. A fetch that answers at once keeps the mount's writes in
# one function, where the two writes of `pending` -- each a copy of the
# write the wrapper of query's unbound props rewrote -- once declared one
# temporary twice.

sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout '5 tests, 0 failures'

-- app.sngl --
import async "sngl:async"
import . "sngl:test"
import . "sngl:ui"
import go "sngl:language/go"

#[go.native("time", "time.Sleep")]
#[go.async]
func sleep(ns int)

// A slow name answers after the quick one asked behind it.
func lookup(name string) async.Result[int] {
    if name == "slow" {
        sleep(400000000)
    } else {
        sleep(10000000)
    }
    return {ok=name.length()}
}

component detail node {
    var name = "apricot"
    var length option[int] = null
    var loading = false
    async.query(on=name, fetch=lookup, :value=length, :pending=loading)
    button #fig(text="fig", @click { name = "fig" })
    button #slow(text="slow", @click { name = "slow" })
}

component dropped node {
    var shown = true
    var answer option[int] = null
    if shown {
        async.query(on="slow", fetch=lookup, :value=answer)
    }
    button #hide(text="hide", @click { shown = false })
}

func testAnswerArrives(t Test, c detail) {
    t.assert(c.loading)
    t.wait(func() => c.length != null, 5000)
    t.assert(c.length == 7)
    t.assert(!c.loading)
}

func testLatestWins(t Test, c detail) {
    c.slow.click()
    c.fig.click()
    t.wait(func() => c.length == 3, 5000)
    t.wait(func() => false, 800)
    t.assert(c.length == 3)
}

component row(name string) node {
    var length option[int] = null
    async.query(on=name, fetch=lookup, :value=length)
    button #pick(text=name, @click { picked = length != null ? length : -1 })
}

var picked = 0

component rows node {
    var names = ["fig", "apricot"]
    for var n = names {
        row #r(name=n)
    }
    button #swap(text="swap", @click { names = ["grape", "fig"] })
}

func testEachRowAsksForItsOwn(t Test, c rows) {
    t.wait(func() => false, 300)
    c.r[0].pick.click()
    t.assert(picked == 3)
    c.r[1].pick.click()
    t.assert(picked == 7)
    c.swap.click()
    t.wait(func() => false, 300)
    c.r[0].pick.click()
    t.assert(picked == 5)
    c.r[1].pick.click()
    t.assert(picked == 3)
}

func quick(name string) async.Result[int] {
    return {ok=name.length()}
}

component quickRow(name string) node {
    var length option[int] = null
    async.query(on=name, fetch=quick, :value=length)
    button #pick(text=name, @click { picked = length != null ? length : -1 })
}

component quickRows node {
    var names = ["fig", "apricot"]
    for var n = names {
        quickRow #r(name=n)
    }
}

func testEachRowAnswersAtOnce(t Test, c quickRows) {
    c.r[1].pick.click()
    t.assert(picked == 7)
}

func testUnmountDrops(t Test, c dropped) {
    c.hide.click()
    t.wait(func() => false, 800)
    t.assert(c.answer == null)
}

window {
    detail
    dropped
    rows
    quickRows
}
